details:
Orbislude – Space Mission Digital Twin Simulator

Orbislude is an early-stage space mission design and digital twin simulation concept developed to make space exploration more accessible and educational.

Our project aims to help users design space missions, explore environmental conditions, and understand how engineering decisions affect mission feasibility.

The proposed platform uses a rule-based decision system that can evaluate mission parameters without depending entirely on artificial intelligence. These parameters include spacecraft mass, energy consumption, communication capabilities, environmental conditions, and mission risks.

Artificial intelligence can optionally support the system by providing more advanced analysis, explanations, and recommendations.

For the Space Mission Design Game challenge, we developed a project concept and presentation demonstrating how users could design a spacecraft, select mission equipment, analyze constraints, and receive understandable feedback.

Our example scenario focuses on a scientific mission in lunar orbit, where players explore trade-offs between spacecraft components and available resources.

Orbislude is currently in the conceptual development stage. Our goal is to develop an interactive educational simulation platform that combines space science, engineering, and explainable decision-making.

This project represents our vision of making space mission planning easier to understand for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.
